name: Example Gadgetmoor Wholesale Co (fictional)
summary: A fictional wholesaler whose reported profit rises every year, while the cash coming in from operations shrinks almost to zero. Profit and cash are telling different stories.
assumptions: All figures are fictional and in millions of USD, except the share price. The same tax rate (25% of pre-tax profit), tax rules and accounting apply to every company. No one-off items, share issues or buybacks. Ratios use Year 3 and the current share price. Simulated for learning; not a real firm.
notes: Net income grew from 39 to 52.5 million, but operating cash flow fell from 38 to 2 million. Profit that does not turn into cash is a warning sign worth investigating.
Possible reasons, as hypotheses only: customers taking longer to pay, unsold stock piling up, or generous accounting choices. The figures alone do not say which.
Free cash flow turned negative in Year 3 and debt rose to cover the gap.
Questions for management: why is cash lagging profit, and when do they expect it to catch up?
